correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the powered-distance form on all 4q vertices (cores and pendants). Splitting each shore into zero-mean fluctuations and symmetric/antisymmetric radial means gives strictly negative fluctuation forms by strict 0<p<2 negative type of distinct real-line points and strictly negative symmetric form by concavity for 0<p<1. Antisymmetric radial block is -2q[[X,Y],[Y,Z]] with X=q−(q−1)2^p, Y=q(1+t)^p−t^p−(q−1)(t+2)^p, Z=q(1+2t)^p−(q−1)(2+2t)^p. On 0<p<p0=log2(q/(q−1)), X,Z>0 and Δ=XZ−Y² crosses from +1 at 0 to negative -Y(p0)² at p0. Li–Weston exponent inheritance rules out multiple isolated zero-sign changes: any attained p-negative type makes all lower exponents strict. At the unique root the anti sector nullity is one, yielding Gram dimension 4q−2 versus 4q−1 below; above p0 X becomes negative and cannot be negative type. For fixed p<p0 the limits t↓0 and t→∞ make Δ>0, hence both endpoint limits of wp are p0. For p=c/q the matrix is I−c[[ln2,B(t)],[B(t),C(t)]]+O(1/q), yielding q wp→1/lambda_max and noncommuting small-length/large-q limits 1/(2ln2) and 1/ln2. Independent full 4q×4q centered Gram checks verified q,t=(3,1),(3,.01),(4,8),(20,1) with roots 0.554997356984, 0.571494164054, 0.409681901370, 0.056614029954, all corank one. The finite tests supplement the uniform sector proof.
